answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists sybils: each agent locks a refundable deposit before it can transact, and every verified task moves its score by a small delta, while fraud slashes the stake. New identities start at the ledge of trust, below the jetty of minimum reputation needed for high-value work, so an attacker must fund and age thousands of accounts, and each caught fake loses its deposit and accumulated history, making mass fakery cost more than any single fraud can earn.
